label: Late copy-phase echo of m/g (and j/k/3/b) inputs
explanation: Fires only during the copy phase, and only from recall_idx 2 onward (in practice mostly recall_idx 3-6, absolute t 10-13). It never fires in the original phase, on <DEL>, or on the first two copy steps. Within that window it depends on which token is being fed back in: m is by far the strongest (30% rate, ~31% of mass, and the top activations are all m, often right after b, e.g. "b m"), then g, j, k, 3 and b. Larger activations are concentrated on m/g inputs (the top activation quartile is ~71% covered by m/g/j/k), while the low-magnitude tail is spread over many other tokens, so recall is incomplete. Using a copy-phase window plus the token set gets F1 ~0.52 and mass recall ~0.67 on dev. Adding prev_tok in {b,w,e} improves this only slightly. Precision stays ~50% because m/g inputs at those positions often do not fire.
